note: Pins what an R1 acceptance environment is. A version that is not here is not a locked version; r1-doctor compares against this file and reports every difference rather than only the ones it expects. Every external dependency records where it comes from, its exact version, and a digest where one exists.

acceptance_platform.note: macOS is a development platform and may not substitute for this (contract R1-09).

image.note: The image identity of the environment R1 was accepted in. An AMI id IS the image digest on AWS: it names one immutable snapshot. A different cloud needs its own equivalent recorded here before a run there counts.

observed_runner.note: BELOW the reference runner below on all three counts. Recorded rather than rounded up: it makes the acceptance run slower and it is the environment the R1 evidence actually came from. A run here is not evidence that the reference runner is unnecessary.

make.note: 3.81 ignores .SHELLFLAGS; no recipe may depend on it

g++.note: the package version is the gcc-defaults metapackage; the compiler it selects reports 13.3.0

yosys.note: synthesis proxies only; not required by the gate

pinned_upstream.note: LLVM and Triton commits are pinned in compiler/pin/; verify_pin.py checks them. This file records that the pin is the authority, not a second copy of it.

not_yet_locked: The development platform (macOS arm64) runs a Triton built from source at a different version from the acceptance wheel; the acceptance environment is the one this file pins
rtl/gen is re-checked only where XLS can run: `make r1-check-generated` reports it as not re-checked unless R1_XLS=1, and on an acceptance environment that needs tools/xls/fetch_xls.sh to have run

mlir.note: tnca-opt and the IR tests build against the distribution's MLIR rather than a personally built one. Ubuntu's LLVM packages are versioned and signed, which is what makes this a lock; a source build at a floating commit would not be. MLIR 18 is NOT enough: it lacks the EffectInstance(effect, OpOperand*, resource) overload the dialect uses, and the build fails to compile rather than silently doing something else.

triton.note: The frontend, from the published wheel rather than a source tree in somebody's home directory. R1-09 forbids referencing a maintainer's existing virtualenv path. 3.8.0 because that is the version the compiler is written against: 3.5.0 installs and imports, and its `ir.operation` has no `get_constant_value`, so the importer cannot read an integer constant. The frontend now falls back to the printed module when the method is absent, but the LOCKED version is the one the tests were written for.

xls.note: The generator for rtl/gen. XLS is a BUILD-time dependency of the RTL and not a runtime one: the generated Verilog is checked in, so simulating and synthesising needs no XLS at all. Regenerating it does, and R1-09 requires that to be a fixed revision run locally or in a container rather than over somebody's ssh.
xls.platform: linux-x64 only; on any other platform xlsgen.py uses the ssh runner and R1_STRICT=1 refuses it
